newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says Bre-X, Barrick agree on Busang.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says Bre-X, Barrick agree on Busang.

text.p: Indonesia said on Monday that Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd and Barrick Gold Corp had agreed on a government proposal for a 25-75 percent split of the spectacular Busang gold find.
"They have reported they can both accept the government suggestion," Umar Said, secretary-general of the Mines and Energy Ministry, told Reuters.
"They are also ready to provide a 10 percent stake to the government. It is good," he said.
The international mining community had watched with apprehension the turmoil over Busang, one of world's largest gold finds, fearing it could make doing business in Indonesia more complicated.
The issue concerned the small Canadian mining firm Bre-X and its stake in the Busang area, which it estimates holds at least 57 million ounces of gold in Indonesia's East Kalimantan province.

Bre-X had sought a partner to provide the funds needed to develop the jungle site on Borneo island. The costs and potential profits are huge -- the current value of the gold amounts to more than $21 billion.

The government had pressed Bre-X to link up with Barrick, one of the world's biggest gold miners and had sought 10 percent of the action. Two members of President Suharto's family are also involved in the long-running saga.
Asked why a decision was not made on the December 4 deadline for an agreement, Umar said the deadline had been extended at the request of Bre-X.

"We didn't make a decision because Bre-X asked for additional time to get the approval of shareholders. This is Canadian law," Umar said. There have been no reports that Bre-X convened a shareholders meeting to discuss the issue.
Umar had earlier said that if the two companies had failed to reach a partnership agreement, the government would explore other ways to expedite development of the Busang find.
He said on Monday the government was consistent with its mining policy but added that its approach with Bre-X was different because the company did not have a contract of work.
"The government has been consistent with its mining policy. But in the case of Bre-X our approach was different because it (Bre-X) does not have a contract of work yet," he said.
Bre-X has yet to be issued with contracts of work for the richest parts of Busang. Its applications are not among the 68 awaiting final approval from Suharto.

Umar said Indonesian Mines and Energy Minister Ida Bagus Sudjana would make a decision on whether to allow Bre-X more time to get shareholders' approval on its agreement with Barrick to develop the Busang property.
"I am waiting for the minister's decision on that. Because the government can or not give an extension. It depends on the government," Umar said.
"In my opinion, there was no need for Bre-X to get approval from its shareholders. But let's wait for the government's decision," he said.
